answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a refundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud or collusion. Reputation and voting weight grow only through accepted tasks, so creating a hundred identities does not create a hundred trusted voices. The attacker must fund each identity separately and risk losing its deposit; the willow team can spot a dawn burst of linked accounts by shared funding patterns, while a vertex of trusted reviewers checks evidence before penalties land.
